definitions.explanation: An honorific expression used to respectfully describe someone coming to a place. Used when speaking about or to people of higher status.

examples.japanese: {先生|せんせい}がお{越|こ}しになりました。
{何時|なんじ}にお{越|こ}しになりますか。
examples.english: What time will you be coming?

examples.japanese: またお{越|こ}しくださいませ。
お{客様|きゃくさま}がお{越|こ}しになるまでに{準備|じゅんび}しておく。
examples.english: I'll get things ready before the guest arrives.

examples.japanese: {遠|とお}い{所|ところ}からお{越|こ}しいただき、ありがとうございます。
examples.english: Thank you for coming from so far away.

notes:
お{越|こ}しになる is a formal honorific ({尊敬語|そんけいご}) for "to come."

KEIGO LEVEL:
This is a respectful expression used to honor the person coming. It elevates the subject's action.

RELATED EXPRESSIONS:
- いらっしゃる: another honorific for come/go/be
- お{見|み}えになる: to arrive (honorific)
- {参|まい}る: to come/go (humble)

COMMON PATTERNS:
- お{越|こ}しください: please come
- お{越|こ}しくださいませ: please come (more polite)
- お{越|こ}しいただく: to have someone come (humble-honorific)
